title: Overwhelmed by Love
paragraphs: He, lost in the thoughts of the beauty met by the Amman shrine, And she, carrying the image of him in her heart’s depths, Are looking forward to meeting again In anxious expectation penance-like.
They won’t sleep, nor would they feel hungry, Like chilli powder sprinkled over the wound Their hearts pained, Which they suppressed by lips held tight together.
For how many days would they keep it undisclosed Without the knowledge of parents?
Would lightning get concealed in darkness? Or would darkness ban lightning tearing through it?
Just as the hero has a confidant right, The heroine also has a beautiful maid for her companion.
“He was startled as to whether you were a goddess; You called him a thief!
With telltale evidences he came to know that you are a human lass Daughter of the earth, flower-like beauty, A woman filled with freshness-- All these you are though,
Like the grass bending towards the stream’s course You are inclined towards love, as if it were your very existence.
You are united as one in emotions and body.”

The companions of the two pile up consolations one after another And yet their hearts remain weighed down. The confidante of the heroine loses on this score While the hero’s friend also doesn’t meet with success.
It is not the failure in a battle fought though, Yet they fail in the task of reducing the momentum of love.

The lady remains thinking about the hero all the time. What was his predicament? The hero with the body of teakwood-- He stood dispirited with emaciated form afflicted by passion’s extreme. Everything seen by the lady reminded her of him While the man found her in everything he saw.

Not knowing what they could do, The male friend and the maid friend invoked the omnipresent God present in each pillar and particle To stand by them and bless them. The answer would be “I am in the heart of the man and the heart of woman In the form of love Though not in the form of the God.”

Lost in love they forget the deed of the day and the inclination for doing too! Confusion, bewilderment, forgetting, Passions’ urge going to the extreme As to drive the partners to suicide Such is the intensity of passion Kaḷaviyal of Tolkāppiyam shows.
Such are the hurdles the lovers need to overcome; But dispirited they are not, And they vow to succeed With their revolve and prowess.

> The vicissitudes of mind > As marking the man and woman > In their clandestine course of love are: > Amorousness, persistent feel of one for the other, > Emaciation of the body, > Giving free vent to experiences of pleasure and pain, > Transgressing the bounds of modesty and propriety, > Every object of sight painfully reminding one > Of the features of the other, > Self-forgetfulness, stupor and death-like anxiety. > > (Poruḷatikāram : Kaḷaviyal, verse 9)
